title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 147
text:
159. Duration of cross-examination must not exceed what the vulnerable witness can reasonably
cope with, taking account of their age/intellectual development, with a total of two hours as
the norm and half a court day at the outside. The witness’s needs may require questioning
to take place over more than one day.
Questioning techniques to avoid

160. Cross-examination techniques using complex vocabulary and syntax, and leading, multi-part
questions, have been demonstrated to mislead and confuse adult witnesses, undermining
the accuracy and completeness of their evidence.
108

161. The Inns of Court College of Advocacy have produced training for advocates which has also
been used by the Judicial College, with a useful set of principles of questioning and conduct,
which should normally be adopted.109
